summary: The admitted C-first wizard wish originally created the same trap and boulder in C and JavaScript, but the first screen differed because trap.c:mkroll_launch unconditionally called newsym after assigning the launch coordinate. JavaScript now supplies the canonical default redraw, and find_random_launch_coord uses the existing mthrowu.c:linedup port for the explicit-launch branch. The complete 106-step wizard-wish recipe now matches, as does the existing 562-step natural rolling-boulder recording.

callers: C: cmd.c:rhack -> wizcmds.c:wiz_wish -> zap.c:makewish -> objnam.c:readobjnam/wizterrainwish -> trap.c:maketrap -> trap.c:mkroll_launch; maketrap consumes find_random_launch_coord’s Boolean result, which itself consumes both isclearpath results.

JavaScript: js/cmd.js:runWishCommand -> js/wizcmds.js:wiz_wish -> js/zap.js:makewish -> js/objnam_readobjnam.js:readobjnam/apply_wizterrainwish -> js/trap.js:maketrap -> makeRollingBoulderLaunch -> findRandomLaunchCoordinate -> clearLaunchPath.
dependencies: trap.c:maketrap already wires the rolling-boulder branch; its return from mkroll_launch is discarded.
mthrowu.c:linedup is an accepted canonical helper now called by the explicit launchplace branch; it preserves C gt.tbx/tby writes.
mkobj.c:mksobj, weight, place_object and stackobj already own boulder construction and placement.
display.c:newsym is already ported as js/display.js:newsym and is supplied through the default trap capability.
source.sourceReview: Read complete upstream trap.c:find_random_launch_coord() (3599-3656), mkroll_launch() (3659-3692), and isclearpath() (3694-3722), plus their trap.c:maketrap() caller (456-588), objnam.c:wizterrainwish() (3554-3916), and objnam.c readobjnam wizard-trap dispatch (4975-4979). find_random_launch_coord returns whether a launch coordinate was found and consumes isclearpath results; its explicit launchplace branch calls mthrowu.c:linedup with boulderhandling=1 and preserves that helper’s gt.tbx/tby effects. mkroll_launch consumes the result to create/place the boulder or fall back to the trap square, assigns launch and mirrored launch2, calls newsym unconditionally, and returns 1 (discarded by maketrap). At diagnosis, makeRollingBoulderLaunch used optional newsym with no default provider; the implementation now calls the capability unconditionally and supplies the canonical display.js:newsym adapter in DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES.

evidence: Saved queue SHA-256 1d8802a0f215249923602217eab5fcec9b1d8c57311d4e82b20e23c60140a093 identifies this v43 case with a screen-cell mismatch at segment 0, step 102, on the newline after the wish text. The first differing cell is row 15, column 64: C has backtick (`), JavaScript has floor (.). The queue reports no RNG mismatch at that boundary.

The admitted C recording’s step 102 draws rn2(5)=0 and rn2(8)=1 in trap.c:find_random_launch_coord, then rnd(2)=2 in next_ident; JavaScript replay of the same 102 input keys records the same three values. C shows “A rolling boulder trap.” and the launch boulder glyph; JavaScript shows the same message but not the new boulder glyph.

A worker-local JavaScript replay through the trap-creation input confirms that the trap is at (61,14), its launch coordinate is (65,14), and a floor boulder object exists at (65,14). The map grid still displays floor at that coordinate. This distinguishes missing newsym display refresh from a missing object, wrong coordinate, or random-call defect.

Baseline source comparison: trap.c:mkroll_launch lines 3683-3691 stores both launch coordinates then calls newsym(ttmp->launch.x, ttmp->launch.y) unconditionally. Before the fix, js/trap.js:makeRollingBoulderLaunch used capability(env, 'newsym')?.(...) and DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES had no newsym provider; objnam_readobjnam.js passes the wizard-wish environment directly to maketrap.
After the source fix, a fresh C recording of the admitted recipe matched all 4,807 RNG calls, 106 screens, 106 cursors, and 16 animation frames.

The existing natural level-generation recording recordings/trap.c/monster-rolling-boulder-trap.session.json matched all 33,322 RNG calls, 562 screens, 562 cursors, and 648 animation frames; its step 555 C RNG trace enters trap.c:find_random_launch_coord.

resolution.implementation: js/trap.js now routes mkroll_launch’s unconditional redraw through DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES.newsym and calls the canonical mthrowu.js:linedup helper for explicit launchplace preflight.
resolution.focusedTest: scripts/trap.test.mjs source-pins the C helper and redraw order.
